creator: Sabine Hossenfelder
title: Astronomers Claim To Have Seen Alien Spacecraft On the Moon
full_text:
A group of astronomers say they've
discovered giant UFOs flying around the
moon.
And they're saying aliens could be here
any minute now. Or as the Daily Mail put
it, scientists issue warning after
spotting more than 20 giant UFOs racing
across the moon. Don't worry, it's
probably nothing. But I also have an
interesting something for you to think
about. Let's have a look. The
astronomers pointed a 15-cm telescope at
the moon, corrected the images for
camera noise, and found some moving
spots which they refer to as
unidentified flying objects. They
calculated that the UFOs are 20 to 40 km
across. Some are shaped like giant
rings, and they travel at up to 11 km
per second. The authors think, quote,
UFOs demonstrate intelligent behavior,
and we believe that the moon serves as a
base for UFOs. They made their
observations in September last year, so
the aliens are taking their time. The
paper is not peer-reviewed and comes
from three researchers in Ukraine. Two
of them already made headlines 4 years
ago when they claimed they'd observed
extremely fast UFOs over Ukraine. Their
own institution subsequently published a
report saying that the authors had an
error in their data analysis. The
distance to the objects was much less
than I thought, so the objects were much
smaller and much slower. The new paper
basically has the same problem. Some of
these objects that they observed are
barely at pixel resolution of their
camera. The authors themselves write
that one object has a size of 2 * 2
pixels. with only one record, you have
no way to determine the distance. They
basically have no data. For all I can
tell, they've observed dust. This
so-called paper is so complete crap.
They probably just wrote this to bait
the Daily Mail. 2 * 2 pixels, aliens are
on the moon. It's exploded my
meter. That said, people have been
reporting strange lights and objects
around the moon for a very long time.
Some of those reports came from the
Apollo astronauts, as you can read in
the documents that the US government
just put out in early August. For
example, during Apollo 12, astronaut
Alan Bean was on the moon and said he
could see particles of light, flashes of
light sailing away into space. He said,
"It looks like some of those things are
escaping the moon." During Apollo 11,
the astronaut saw some region near a
crater light up. During the Apollo 17
flyover, geologist Harrison Schmitt
suddenly said, "Hey, I just saw a flash
on the lunar surface." There have been
thousands of reports of reported moon
irregularities.
Some of those might be meteorite impacts
or sunlight reflections, but some of
them can't be explained that way. For
example, in 2007, an Italian amateur
astronomer filmed a dark circular object
apparently crossing the surface of the
moon. 2020, someone else near Montreal
filmed three elongated objects. In March
2024, a German astronomer filmed a fast
dark object crossing the lunar disc that
he could not identify. Yeah, no, I don't
think any of these were alien
spacecraft, but I do think it's very
possible that sometime in the past
billion years or so, extraterrestrials
came by our solar system and had a look
at our planet. And they'd most likely
have done that from the moon. Maybe
their technology is indeed still there.
And this is just something I made up. In
2013, two physicists argued in a
peer-reviewed paper that we should
search for alien artifacts on the moon.
Their reasoning was that the lunar
surface changes incredibly slowly, which
is both great for observations and great
for preservation of whatever was doing
the observation. They estimate that an
object a few tens of meters across could
take hundreds of millions of years to
disappear through impacts. Concretely,
they say we might find instrumentation
deliberately installed to monitor Earth
or a dormant probe awaiting contact.
This search still hasn't been done. You
also don't have a database dedicated to
moon anomalies. Anomalous moon
observations are usually lumped together
with general UAP sightings. I think it'd
be a good idea to keep these separate
because if you're looking to explain
them, these explanations would have to
be very different. I mean, look, the
European Union has a database for potato
types. I feel like moon UFOs could get
at least a spreadsheet. In other news, a
physicist just wrote a paper claiming
that some of the observed unidentified
anomalous phenomena are dark matter.
Chances are, if we ever find actual
aliens, physicists will explain their
previously unknown type of dark matter.

sources.quote: I suddenly saw a fast, bright something flitting through the picture
sources.explanation: Voltmer explicitly describes the object he saw as bright, rather than dark.

sources.quote: Due to the Brightness it could have been the ISS.
sources.explanation: The astronomer noted the object was bright enough to be mistaken for the International Space Station.

sources.quote: Even then, birds tend to appear dark rather than bright.
sources.explanation: Voltmer contrasts the bright object he filmed with birds, which he says appear dark in those conditions.

sources.quote: Planetary scientist Elliot Sefton-Nash also spoke to BILD: 'The object looks like a series of low-Earth orbit satellites with orbits close together.'
Sefton-Nash has pointed to Starlink as the most likely explanation
sources.explanation: This supports the note's claim that Sefton-Nash suggested the object resembled Starlink satellites.

notes.note: Dedicated lunar-anomaly databases already exist, separate from UAP catalogs. NASA's 1968 'Chronological Catalog of Reported Lunar Events' and Cameron's 1978 Lunar Transient Phenomena Catalog compile transient lunar phenomena independently of UAP sighting data.

sources.quote: The term was created by Patrick Moore in his co-authorship of NASA Technical Report R-277 Chronological Catalog of Reported Lunar Events, published in 1968.
sources.explanation: Confirms the existence of the 1968 NASA catalog cited in the note.

sources.quote: Two extensive catalogs of transient lunar phenomena exist,[1][2] with the most recent tallying 2,254 events going back to the 6th century.
sources.explanation: Supports the claim that dedicated databases for lunar anomalies (TLPs) exist independently of general UAP data.

sources.quote: Lunar transient phenomena catalog This catalog lists 1468 descriptions of observed lunar transient phenomena reported in the literature.
sources.explanation: Directly supports the existence of Winifred Cameron's 1978 catalog cited in the note.
